originalGroup.material:
A paper crown for Grandpa

Grandpa's birthday was on Sunday. My little sister wanted to buy him a crown. "He tells the best stories," she said. "He should be a ____1____."

We went to a toy shop, but every crown was too small. My sister looked ____2____. Then I remembered the large sheet of gold paper at home. Perhaps we could make one.

We measured Grandpa's old hat to find the right ____3____. I drew a long strip, and my sister added stars. We cut it out and joined the ends with tape. The crown looked beautiful, but it fell over when we put it on the table. The paper was too ____4____.

Mum suggested putting a strip of card inside. This made the crown ____5____ enough to stand. My sister wanted to cover it with more stars, but we left a small space at the front for a ____6____: "Our Story King."

On Sunday, Grandpa opened our box. He put the crown on and laughed. It was larger than a toy crown, but it ____7____ him perfectly.

After tea, we asked for a story. Grandpa began, "Once there were two clever children who made something with their own ____8____."

My sister smiled. The crown had cost almost nothing, but Grandpa kept it on all afternoon. Later, he put it on his bookshelf, ____9____ his favourite storybook. When we visited the next week, it was still there. We had not found the right present in a shop. We had ____10____ it together.

originalGroup.material:
The picnic place

We planned a bicycle picnic beside the lake. On Saturday morning, the sky was clear. Dad packed sandwiches, and I put apples in a bag. My sister brought a small ____1____ so we could sit on the grass.

Halfway to the lake, dark clouds appeared. Then rain began to fall. We left the road and stopped at an empty bus shelter. Its roof kept us ____2____, but we could not continue our ride immediately.

I was angry with the weather. "The day is ____3____," I said.

Dad looked at his watch. It was nearly lunchtime. "The lake will still be there another day," he said. "The sandwiches are here ____4____."

We sat on the bench and opened the food. My sister spread her cloth over our knees like a tiny table. A woman waiting for the bus smiled at us. We offered her an apple, and she showed us a photograph of the lake in ____5____. The water was frozen, and snow covered the path.

"I've only seen it in summer," I said. Her picture made me want to ____6____ again in another season.

After lunch, the rain stopped. We checked the road and decided to ride ____7____ instead of continuing to the lake. There would be enough time to dry our clothes before visiting Grandma.

At home, my sister drew our picnic. She included the shelter, bench and woman with the photograph. The lake was not in the picture, but our day was. I had thought a good picnic needed one ____8____ place. Now I knew it also needed food and people I enjoyed being ____9____. We would try the lake again, but I did not want to ____10____ the picnic we had already had.

originalGroup.material:
Pip and the blue glove

My aunt's dog Pip liked carrying things. He brought slippers to the door and sometimes took a newspaper into the garden. When Aunt May said he could help find lost things, I wanted to ____1____ him.

I placed a blue glove behind a chair while Pip waited in the kitchen. Then Aunt May let him smell its partner. He ran into the room, looked around and returned with a ____2____. It was blue too, but it belonged on my foot.

I laughed. "He has found the wrong thing!"

Aunt May did not call him a bad dog. She took the sock gently and showed him the glove again. "We need to make the task ____3____," she said.

This time, I placed the glove where part of it was ____4____ beside the chair. Pip found it quickly. We praised him and stopped after a few short tries, before he became ____5____.

Later, I could not find my own cap. I almost called Pip, but the garden gate was open and a delivery van was outside. Aunt May asked me to keep Pip ____6____ while she closed the gate. A game did not matter more than keeping him safe.

I found the cap myself, ____7____ the newspaper. Pip had not hidden it; I had put the paper on top of it.

That afternoon taught me two things. Helping a dog learn required ____8____, not just a loud command. And before blaming someone else for a lost object, I should ____9____ where I had left it. Pip carried his toy to me, and I put away my notebook. Nothing was missing now; we could simply ____10____.
